claims.text: In situ HR-TEM heating can investigate the atomic-scale thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will maintain atomic-scale structural integrity at elevated temperatures.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit minimal coarsening during heating.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit minimal phase separation during heating.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Lattice distortions, defect formation, and early precipitate nucleation can indicate breakdown of an entropy-stabilized phase.
High configurational entropy in multicomponent high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles kinetically suppresses atomistic rearrangements at elevated temperatures.
Sluggish diffusion in multicomponent high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles suppresses coarsening and phase separation at elevated temperatures.
In situ TEM can directly visualize atomic-scale structural stability during heating.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will show negligible grain growth up to an elevated-temperature threshold.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will show no new diffraction spots attributable to secondary-phase formation up to an elevated-temperature threshold.
The onset temperature for structural changes in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will be higher than in conventional binary or ternary nanoparticles.
Conventional alloy nanoparticles or lower-component systems typically undergo significant coarsening at lower temperatures under comparable conditions.
Conventional alloy nanoparticles or lower-component systems typically begin phase separation at lower temperatures under comparable conditions.
Electron-beam effects can obscure or alter thermally induced atomistic changes during in situ TEM.
In situ TEM is better suited to detecting distinct transformations than very gradual atomic diffusion.
